FOSDEM 2027 — Open Smart Home Devroom

Call for Papers · Brussels, Belgium · 30–31 January 2027 · Exact devroom day TBA

Connecting ecosystems. Returning control.

The Smart Homes Devroom will give FOSDEM a place where the full open-source smart-home stack comes together: not as competing islands, but as one connected technical ecosystem.

Attendees should leave with a clearer understanding of how these technologies complement each other — and how open source can return meaningful control of the connected home to the people who live in it.

Building an open smart home involves much more than choosing a home automation platform. It requires devices and embedded software, communication protocols, message brokers, orchestration tools, data storage, observability, energy management, edge intelligence and reliable infrastructure. These components are often presented separately, even though their real value emerges when they work together.

The Smart Homes Devroom will connect these layers and demonstrate how open, interoperable, local-first and vendor-independent digital homes can be built in practice.

If your work helps explain how one part of the stack fits into the wider ecosystem, how different technologies integrate, or how open source can deliver more control and long-term value to users, we would like to hear from you.

What We’re Looking For

We welcome submissions covering topics including, but not limited to:

  • Platforms & automation: home automation platforms, architectures, orchestration, workflow tools and integrations.
  • Devices & embedded systems: open hardware, embedded systems, sensors, actuators and device firmware.
  • Interoperability & messaging: Matter, Thread, Zigbee, Z-Wave, MQTT, event-driven infrastructure, protocol bridges and gateways.
  • Infrastructure & self-hosting: homelabs, message brokers, storage, networking, monitoring, observability and data visualisation.
  • Sensing & edge intelligence: local voice assistants, edge AI, computer vision, presence and occupancy detection.
  • Energy: energy monitoring and optimisation, solar integration, batteries, smart EV charging and energy-aware automation.
  • Privacy, security & resilience: local-first and offline operation, security, reliability, long-term maintainability and liberation of cloud-dependent devices.
  • Real-world implementations: integrations across different layers, failures, trade-offs, migrations and lessons learned.
  • Emerging technologies: projects and ideas that could shape the future of open smart homes.

We particularly encourage presentations that explain the problem a project or technical approach solves, demonstrate integrations between open technologies, discuss standards and real-world interoperability, explain architectural choices and trade-offs, share operational experience and lessons learned, or provide reusable knowledge to the wider community.

Project introductions are welcome, especially where they help attendees understand an important part of the wider ecosystem. Proposals should go beyond a feature overview and explain the problem the project solves, where it fits in the smart-home stack, how it complements or integrates with other technologies, and what value it brings to users seeking more open, interoperable and controllable homes.

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for maintainers, core contributors and experienced practitioners who can share first-hand knowledge of a project, standard, integration, architecture or real-world implementation.

Real-world implementations are welcome when they reveal lessons, patterns or integration approaches that are useful to the wider community and help others build more open, reliable and interoperable smart-home environments.

The audience will include people from different parts of the open-source ecosystem, with varying levels of familiarity with smart-home technologies. Talks should therefore provide enough context to be understandable beyond a project’s own community, while still offering meaningful technical insight.

Speakers should explain where their technology fits, how it relates to other parts of the stack, what value it brings to the wider ecosystem and end users, and what attendees should take away from the session. The aim is not to simplify the subject, but to make the talk accessible across neighbouring technical communities.

Talk Format

Standard talk — 30-minute slot

25 minutes presentation · 3 minutes Q&A · 2 minutes changeover.

For technical deep dives, architectures, integrations, project developments and substantial real-world lessons.

Short talk — 15-minute slot

10 minutes presentation · 3 minutes Q&A · 2 minutes changeover.

For focused technical topics, compact demos, small projects, experiments, one strong idea or a concise lesson learned.

Choose the format that best fits your proposal. The organisers may suggest the other format when building the final programme.

How to Submit

Talks will be submitted through the official FOSDEM 2027 Pretalx system. The direct submission link will be added here as soon as FOSDEM opens the talk CFP, expected around 27 October 2026.

Your submission should include:

  • Your name and short biography
  • Contact information
  • Talk title
  • A concise abstract explaining the problem, technical approach, ecosystem value and what attendees will learn
  • Intended audience and assumed knowledge
  • Your preferred format: Standard Talk or Short Talk
  • Relevant project, repository or documentation links where applicable
CFP deadline: 24 November 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Technical, Open and Non-Commercial

The Smart Homes Devroom is strictly non-commercial. Vendor-neutral technical contributions are welcome, but product pitches, sales presentations and marketing-led talks are not.

Proposals will be evaluated on their technical substance, openness, relevance, originality and value to the FOSDEM community.

Volunteering

A team of six volunteers has already committed to help staff the Smart Homes Devroom throughout the day. Additional help is welcome. If you would like to support speaker preparation, room operations, timekeeping or transitions, contact the organisers.

FOSDEM itself also runs on volunteers. You can register through the official FOSDEM volunteer site.
